$comment: Single source of truth for scope (Lesson 8). Every feature carries the triple: behavior + verification + state, plus evidence. Only the checker/verification script flips status to passing/done (Lesson 9). Replace these placeholders with real features whose verification is a runnable command. readyForCheck means the complete feature-level behavior is implemented with green verification and complete evidence; partial maker checkpoints leave it false. attempts/maxAttempts timeboxes failed checker review cycles: the checker increments attempts on REJECT and blocks at the limit, while maker checkpoints do not consume the budget. `context` is the handoff INTO implementation: the 1-3 files the feature touches, plus one line the implementer would otherwise rediscover. The planner already has to name those files to size the feature (feature-decomposition.md Step 3) — recording them is what stops the next agent re-reading the codebase to learn what the last one already knew. `evidence` is a LIST OF RUNS, not a paragraph: [{date, run: red|green, cmd, result}]. A plain string still works for older lists, but the list form keeps each line readable in a diff and lets the red-run check be exact instead of a regex over prose. `behavior` and `falsifier` are ONE SENTENCE each — if either needs a paragraph, that is the feature being two features (feature-scope-smell). Each feature also carries kind (build|prove) and falsifier: the specific wrong implementation its verification would fail on. A verification whose falsifier you cannot name does not discriminate — see docs/reference/test-authoring.md.

features.name: Baseline green
features.behavior: Project installs deps, runs the baseline gate to green, and starts from a clean checkout
features.falsifier: a gate that exits 0 without running anything — or one that runs a failing step and swallows it, which the bash version did — the baseline must be able to go red

features.name: First real feature (REPLACE ME)
features.behavior: Replace with the first concrete behavior the agent should implement
features.verification: REPLACE with a runnable command that proves this behavior, e.g. npm test -- feature-x

context.note: One line the implementer would otherwise have to rediscover: the seam, the gotcha, the existing thing to reuse. Add context.packet only when the planner materializes a digest-bound packet for a non-obvious seam.

features.falsifier: REPLACE with the wrong implementation this command catches, e.g. 'returns the input unchanged' or 'rounds half-up instead of half-even'

features.name: Cross-service integration verification for feat-002 (REPLACE ME)
features.behavior: A full-pipeline check that the feature works across the microservice boundary — contract holds between the services involved (Lesson 10)
features.verification: REPLACE with the microservice integration / contract command, e.g. npm run test:contract or docker compose up + a cross-service flow test
features.falsifier: REPLACE with the cross-boundary defect this catches, e.g. 'service A serialises the field as a string while B expects a number'
